threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the overground' while riding the Dalston route. Everyone's side-eyeing you in the carriage.
Last night on the 59, I saw a guy passionately reciting Shakespeare to a bemused group. Only in Brixton would you find late-night poetry on a bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the sound of the late-night kebab shop's orders blended with the distant sirens. That's when I knew this chaos was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you hit a strip of greenery between U-Bahn stations, where random parties sprout up on weekends, complete with techno and grill smoke.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know the best time to dodge the BART delays—another round of brake overheating and folks still think they can make it downtown on time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy reciting Shakespeare on the bus this morning. Muni moments like that remind me why I love this city, even with the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hipster bars, but the real charm is in the corner bakeries serving fresh cocas de recapte that locals swear by.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they awkwardly try to navigate the Mercat de l'Abaceria, scanning the stalls like it's a museum exhibit.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep saying 'the tube' when everyone knows it's just 'the Overground' around here. And you still look confused by the bus routes.
Caught the N47 last night; two blokes were arguing over who'd seen the most obscure band at The Old Kent. Typical South London midnight vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a family of wild boars crossing my street, completely unbothered by the traffic. Just another day in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble upon a spontaneous rooftop yoga session while the scent of currywurst wafts through the air. It's a unique blend of Berlin life.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to pack snacks for a BART delay—it's never just a minute. This week, I saw folks munching chips while waiting for rescue.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 with a guy singing off-key about the weather while a woman next to him started selling homemade masks. Classic SF mashup.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia only sleeps; locals know the real nightlife blooms in quiet squares after 10 PM.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still ask for a ‘café con leche’ instead of just a ‘café’. The locals have their shortcuts down.
